newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Tomkins performs U-turn on buybacks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tomkins performs U-turn on buybacks.

text.p: British diversified industrial group Tomkins Plc staged a policy U-turn on Monday, announcing a share buyback as part of plans to increase shareholder value.

Tomkins, whose shares have underperformed the market since January when it ruled out a buyback in favour of acquisitions, said it planned to buy back up to 100 million pounds ($169.1 million) of shares within three months.
Shares in the company, whose baking and specialised engineering activities include the British "Hovis" bread brand and Smith & Wesson handguns, quickly rose 19 pence to 283p.
Investors also took heart from Tomkin's 33.7 percent rise in annual profits and the promise of another year of growth in earnings and dividends.
Executive chairman Gregory Hutchings said Tomkins had opted for a buyback because soaring markets were pricing major acquisitions out of reach.

"We are in a bull market. Very large unrelated acquisitions are expensive and we don't think we are going to get decent returns from those. So while this bull market continues, we will re-adjust our sights and make smaller add-ons where we find synergy benefits," Hutchings told Reuters in a phone interview.
Tomkins said it would ask shareholders at the next general meeting to renew its authority to buy back up to 10 percent of its shares.
"We will hand back cash until the time when it becomes beneficial to look for large acquisitions," Hutchings said.
Tomkins, whose annual pretax profits rose in line with market expectations to 431.8 million pounds on sales of 4.59 billion, raised its cash pile by 222.5 million to 617 million.
The company's strong cash flow enabled it to raise the total dividend by 15 percent to 11.45 pence, paying a final dividend of 8.39 pence.
Tomkins said it had got off to a strong start this year, with orders strong across the group and major markets continuing to expand.
Hutchings said Tomkins was particularly encouraged by results at newly-acquired automotive and industrial products firm Gates Corp, bought last year for one billion dollars.
"Gates is going really well...We've raised margins there from 7.4 percent to 8.8 percent and generated cash out of it so we're in good shape," he said.

Hutchings, who said 55 percent of Tomkins' group reveue was dollar-denominated, said the company was well protected against the pound's recent strength by 12-month hedging agreements locking the pound at $1.62.
Despite his caution on acquisitions, Hutchings said Tomkins still had room to make add-on acquisitions, possibly in the construction products and consumer products areas.
Last year, Tomkins bought Gates and followed up with the complementary 372-million pound acquisition of Stant Corp, a U.S. supplier of windscreens and other car components.

"This transaction was completed after the year end and the combined operation offers us attractive growth opportunities...Our result will be boosted by a full-year contribution from Gates and the first-time benefit from Stant," Tomkins said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 4017 ($ = 0.591 British Pounds)
